content.name: p
children: Upgrade the API and controller as one reviewed change.

content.name: h2
children: Before upgrading

content.name: p
children: Read the target release's upgrade notes. Save your current chart version, values,
and policy manifests in your deployment repository. Keep database recovery
procedures separate: rolling back a controller does not reverse committed SQL.

content.name: p
children: Set the exact release you reviewed, for example

children.name: code
children: VERSION=0.11.0
. Render and
review its resources using your existing values:

content.name: Fence
children:
VERSION=0.11.0
helm template pgroles-operator oci://ghcr.io/thepartly/charts/pgroles-operator \
  --version "$VERSION" --namespace pgroles-system --include-crds \
  --values values.yaml > operator-rendered.yaml

content.name: p
children: Check the image, resource limits, admission policies, and CRD changes. The API is

children.name: code
children: v1alpha1
with no conversion webhook. Do not assume an older controller can read
newer resources or approvals.

content.name: h2
children: Update CRDs, then the controller

content.name: p
children: Helm installs CRDs but does not upgrade them. Extract the CRDs from the

children.name: strong
children: same
chart version
, inspect the diff, then apply them before upgrading:

content.name: Fence
children:
set -euo pipefail
helm show crds oci://ghcr.io/thepartly/charts/pgroles-operator \
  --version "$VERSION" > operator-crds.yaml
test -s operator-crds.yaml
kubectl diff --server-side -f operator-crds.yaml

content.name: p

children.name: code
children: kubectl diff
exits 1 when differences exist. After reviewing them, run:

content.name: Fence
children:
kubectl apply --server-side -f operator-crds.yaml
helm upgrade pgroles-operator oci://ghcr.io/thepartly/charts/pgroles-operator \
  --version "$VERSION" --namespace pgroles-system --values values.yaml --wait

content.name: h2
children: Moving from 0.10 to 0.11

children.name: li
children: Apply all five version-matched CRDs before starting the new controller. The
plan schema adds the optional diagnostic

children.name: code
children: passwordSourceDigest
field; it
does not replace the approval digest or authorize execution.

children.name: li
children: Wildcard revocations now retain each concrete object's grantor. Plans can
contain more revoke statements, and changed effects require fresh approval.
Review replacement plans and the executor's authority to act as each grantor.

children.name: li
children: Plan creation now distinguishes interrupted creates from collisions with
existing plans. Changes to password source versions also replace stale plans; review
and approve the replacement when manual approval is required.

children.name: li
children: A policy-level

children.name: code
children: role_pattern
now supplies the naming convention for schemas
that omit their own pattern. Previously ignored top-level patterns in CLI
manifests now take effect. Review generated role names and the resulting plan
before applying; keep explicit schema patterns where names must stay unchanged.
The old Kubernetes API pruned the unsupported policy-level field, so reapply
it after upgrading the CRDs. Existing resources may also contain schema-level
patterns inserted by the previous CRD's defaulting. Inspect the live resource:
those values still override the policy pattern. Remove an override only when
you intend that schema to inherit the new convention. Inspect outstanding
candidates and plans after the upgrade; review any replacement plans before
approving them.

children.name: li
children: Reconciliation concurrency still defaults to one. Retain that setting unless
measurements justify increasing it.

content.name: p
children: The CLI's new Markdown report fingerprint identifies report content. It is not
an approval digest or a database identity check; approve operator plans through
the existing plan workflow.

content.name: h2
children: Moving from 0.9 to 0.10

children.name: li
children: Open plans need fresh approval because the effect digest encoding changed to
v3. Inspect replacement plans; old decisions do not transfer.

children.name: li
children: Replace deprecated

children.name: code
children: mode: plan
with

children.name: code
children: mode: observe

children.name: li
children: Database grant targets must include

children.name: code
children: object.name
, matching the connected database.

children.name: li
children: Review declared memberships in external roles: they now take effect.

children.name: li
children: Adopt-mode schema-owner transfers require a separate explicit opt-in.

children.name: li
children: Validate policy size limits and UTC whole-second

children.name: code
children: password_valid_until
values.

children.name: li
children: Update JSON consumers for tagged default-privilege

children.name: code
children: scope
. Bundle output is

children.name: code
children: pgroles.bundle_plan.v2
; ordinary diff JSON remains unversioned, so pin its
producer version.

content.name: p
children: Version 0.10.1 changes each controller's default reconciliation concurrency to
one. Keep that default until measurements support a higher value; see

children.name: Link
children: running the operator

content.name: h2
children: Verify after upgrading

content.name: p
children: For each policy, inspect conditions, observed generation, current plan, and
warnings. For apply-mode convergence, require the observed generation to match,

children.name: code
children: Ready=True
with reason

children.name: code
children: Reconciled
, and

children.name: code
children: Drifted=False
; no plan should remain
Pending, Approved, or Applying. An Applied plan may remain referenced.

content.name: p
children: Observe mode and manual approval can legitimately have pending changes. Review
replacement plans before approving, then test allowed and denied operations as
actual service identities. Check operator restarts and inspection latency.

content.name: p
children: If the upgrade fails, inspect

children.name: Link
children: troubleshooting
before retrying. Reverting the chart alone neither downgrades CRDs nor undoes SQL.

frontmatter.title: Upgrading the operator
frontmatter.description: Upgrade version-matched CRDs and the controller, review changed approvals, and verify convergence.
